title: Student Handoff — importing the monitoring workbook
story: Student Handoff is the first step of the lifecycle: the Academic Coordinator's AC Student Monitoring workbook (Excel) arrives from outside the portal and Graduate School staff import it. The import creates each student, the program and the curriculum, marks the subjects already completed, and gives each new student a portal login. The same screen keeps every uploaded file, so an upload can be traced and its conflicts reviewed later.

The sample workbooks of the project are in the folder Documents/Monitoring_Sheets/Ready_To_Import (one per program). This case uses the MSN (Master of Science in Nursing) sample, trimmed to two new students with time-stamped names and new ID numbers, so the demonstration data are not touched and a re-run does not collide. The workbook layout is the AC template: PROGRAM in cell A1, one student per row, the AY entry on every row and a unit value in each completed subject cell.
accounts: Imports the workbook and reviews the result

MSN, 18 curriculum subjects, all marked completed in the sheet

steps.text: Sign in as **staff@usls.edu.ph** and open **1 · Student Handoff** under Lifecycle Workflows. The page is titled **Student Handoff** (Who uses it: GS Staff). The main panel is **Import from monitoring sheet**: a drop area for the .xlsx file (Drag & drop your .xlsx here, or Browse files), the button **Import students**, an **Upload history** list and a panel **Onboarding report & Dean approval**. A side note, **How this works**, says that official source data arrives as a file and that a NOTE of LOA, AWOL or withdrawn on a new student is taken in as their standing.

shots.caption: Student Handoff: the import panel, upload history and the onboarding report for the Dean.

steps.text: Select **Browse files** and choose the workbook. The file name appears in the drop area with **Choose a different file** and the **Import students** button becomes available.

shots.caption: The workbook chosen, ready to import.

steps.text: Select **Import students**. A green result reads: Imported 2 new student(s) and refreshed AY/YR for 0 student(s) from the MSN monitoring sheet (0 already in system or needing verification, 0 conflict(s)). 2 new student portal account(s) created. Counters show 2 New, 0 AY/YR refreshed, 0 Existing / skipped, 36 Cell changes, 0 Conflicts, 18 Subjects and the program MSN. **Imported students (sample)** lists Alma and Ben with their stage and 18/18 subjects. **Open Monitoring Sheet** and **View Students** buttons follow.

shots.caption: Import result: two new students, 36 cell changes, no conflicts.

parts.title: Part B - Upload history and the onboarding report

steps.text: Select **View upload history**. Every uploaded workbook is listed with its file name, program, number of students, date, the status **Validated** and a **Backup** download button. The text says every uploaded workbook is preserved and a version can be opened to review conflicts between its values and the current record.

shots.caption: Upload history: each workbook is preserved with a Validated status and a backup download.

steps.text: Scroll to **Onboarding report & Dean approval**. Each import batch appears as a card (program, number of students, new students, file name, status **Draft**) with a checklist that the system derives from the import: Admission handoff recorded, Student profiles created from the import, Program assignment confirmed, and Validation issues resolved. The button **Send onboarding report to Dean** is enabled only when the checklist is complete. This walkthrough does not send it; the Dean's side of that report is outside this case.

shots.caption: Onboarding report: a derived checklist for the import batch, with Send onboarding report to Dean.

parts.title: Part C - Importing the same file again is safe

steps.text: Reload the page, choose the same workbook again and select **Import students**. The result now reads: Imported 0 new student(s) ... (2 already in system or needing verification, 0 conflict(s)). The counters show 0 New and 2 Existing / skipped, and a panel **Already in the system** lists Alma and Ben with the message that these students were already added, so they were not imported again. Nothing is duplicated and nothing is overwritten.

shots.caption: Second import of the same file: 0 new, 2 already in the system, nothing duplicated.

steps: Each upload is still preserved in the upload history, including a repeat of the same file, and a repeat appears in the onboarding report as its own batch with 0 students and an incomplete checklist, so it cannot be sent to the Dean by mistake.

parts.title: Part D - The imported students on the Monitoring Sheet

steps.text: Select **Open Monitoring Sheet** in the import result. The Monitoring Sheet opens on the program MSN. The two new students are at the bottom of the grid with every subject cell Completed (C), AY entry 22-23.

shots.caption: The imported students on the MSN grid: every subject completed, as in the workbook.

steps.text: Select the pencil beside Alma Walkthru<stamp>. The record panel shows IDNO, program MSN, AY entry 22-23, the badge **Imported** and 18 of 18 curriculum subjects completed (54/54 units), with the source of every row shown as **Imported**. Close the panel. Editing and adding rows from here is covered in {case:monitoring-sheet}.

shots.caption: An imported student's record: every row is marked Imported.

notes: The platform does not replace AIMS. The workbook is an export of the Academic Coordinator's monitoring sheet; official grades and enrollment stay in AIMS.
New students get a portal login with the shared demonstration password.
A later upload that disagrees with a value entered or corrected in the portal is held for review as a conflict instead of overwriting it.
Only the sample workbook layout (the AC template) was tested.
